I am 57 years old, and I have been farming my family's land in Quzhou for over forty years. This land is good black soil on the North China Plain, and the weather here has always suited the wheat-maize rotation. I have about 8 mu of land, and I am not going to gamble with new crops at my age—winter wheat followed by summer maize is what I know, what the grain station will buy, and what puts food on the table. 

Last year I planted Lüyuan 502 wheat and Dēnghǎi 605 maize, and the yields were steady. I will buy the same improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed from the township supply store again. For the wheat, after the maize harvest I will run the rotary tiller to break up the stalks and prepare the seedbed. I will put down basal compound fertilizer and then sow before the winter freeze. I will irrigate four times—winter irrigation is essential to protect the seedlings from the cold, plus spring top-dressing water and two more irrigations at jointing and grain-filling. I will spray insecticide, herbicide, and fungicide about four times total because the diseases and weeds have been getting worse with the warm winters.

For the summer maize, as soon as the wheat comes off in early June, I will plant the maize directly into the wheat stubble with no-tillage. There is no time to waste—the growing season is short. I will fertilize at sowing and irrigate twice, once at the seedling stage and once at the big trumpet stage. Three pesticide applications should be enough for the maize borer and weeds. This is the system that works. I do not need to take risks.
